headline: Last session: Indian benchmarks snapped winning streak as crude oil prices surged to six-month highs

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging crude oil prices hitting six-month highs weighed heavily on Indian equity markets.
Concerns over global inflation and rising energy costs drove widespread profit-taking.
Key benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty fell 2% over the week, snapping their recent winning streak.
Corporate earnings reports showed mixed results, impacted by external sector pressures.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty dropped around 2% over the week as Brent crude oil prices neared $117 per barrel.
JK Cement reported a 7.8% increase in Q2 net profit to Rs 173 crore.
BPCL reported a 22.5% decline in Q2 profit to Rs 4,993 crore due to fuel price freezes.
Adani Enterprises was among the major losers in the recent weekly market wrap.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian benchmark indices recorded weekly losses of about 2% driven by surging global crude oil prices. Corporate earnings showed mixed results with JK Cement reporting profit growth while BPCL faced margin pressure. The Indian stock market is closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 26 October.
